summary: The three K_D→K^{↔}/Q prose cleanups are stylistically coherent with the prior R5 direction, the `tests/test_numerics/test_wlc_bb84.py` expectation change from `1.0` to `0.5` is correct for the per-signal convention implemented in `qkdx/numerics/wlc.py:483`, and the new AD fill CSV is numerically well-behaved: `E_R^PPT` decreases monotonically while `log_neg/E_R^PPT` increases monotonically across the sampled AD points. However, the new AD memo/plot make a fundamental scientific overclaim: they treat the Choi-state quantity computed by `e_r_channel_ppt` as a proven upper bound on the channel two-way key capacity `K^{↔}` for qubit amplitude damping, but the cited chain does not justify that step and one inequality in the memo is explicitly reversed. That breaks the memo’s main conclusion and makes the current `[SYN]` label unsound.

issues.description: The memo’s central claim `K^{↔}(N_AD) ≤ E_R^PPT(J_N)` is not established by the cited reasoning. The text first states `K^{↔} ≤ D_d^{↔}` at line 55, but that direction is false: distillable entanglement is not an upper bound on distillable key; private states can have key without comparable distillable entanglement (Horodecki et al., PRL 94, 160502, https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.94.160502). More importantly, `e_r_channel_ppt` computes REE/PPT-REE of the Choi state, while PLOB distinguishes channel REE from Choi-state REE (`E_R(N) = sup_ρ E_R[(I⊗N)(ρ)] ≥ E_R(J_N)`) and only collapses to a Choi-state converse for teleportation-simulable / teleportation-covariant channels; amplitude damping is explicitly not teleportation-covariant (Nature Comm. 8:15043, https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms15043; WTB 2017 DOI https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.2017.2648825). Horodecki’s `2⊗2` PPT=SEP result (https://doi.org/10.1016/S0375-9601(97)00416-7) only upgrades `E_R^PPT(J_N)` to `E_R(J_N)` for the Choi state; it does not prove a converse for the channel key capacity. As written, the memo title, the `Q ≤ K^{↔} ≤ E_R^PPT` plot title, and the fill-script status message all silently upgrade a numerical Choi-state observation into a channel-capacity bound.
issues.suggestion: Remove all statements that present `E_R^PPT(J_N)` as a strict or proven upper bound on AD channel `K^{↔}`. Recast the memo as a data note about the Choi-state quantity only, or replace the argument with a valid channel-level converse (for example a channel REE / amortized REE / squashed-entanglement bound) and prove why the Choi-state value is the right channel quantity for this family before restoring the bound. The `[SYN]` tag should be downgraded until that bridge is supplied.

issues.description: The stated asymptotic ratio `log_neg/E_R^PPT → log₂(3)/log₂(2) ≈ 2.25` is internally inconsistent and numerically wrong. `log₂(2)=1`, so `log₂(3)/log₂(2)=log₂(3)≈1.585`, not `2.25`. The sampled data in the attached CSV instead approach about `2.236` by `γ=0.95`. Since no derivation is given, this should not be written as a named logarithmic constant.
issues.suggestion: Keep this as a purely empirical statement only, e.g. `the sampled ratio increases monotonically and appears to approach ~2.24 near γ→1`, or supply an actual derivation for the limit before naming a constant. Do not attach the current `log₂(3)/log₂(2)` formula.

round_recommendation: Rework the AD memo/plot around a valid channel-level converse or downgrade them to Choi-state numerical observations, then fix the ratio-limit line. The prose replacements and WLC unit-test correction can remain.
